unit.title: Ojalá & Como Si
unit.subtitle: Wishing with ojalá and speaking hypothetically with como si

grammar.title: Two expressions that live entirely in the subjunctive
grammar.intro: Some of the most expressive Spanish hides in two little words. Ojalá (“I hope / if only”) takes a different subjunctive tense depending on how likely the wish is — from a hopeful future to a past regret. Como si (“as if”) is even stricter: it always takes a past subjunctive, because it introduces a comparison that isn't true. Neither one ever accepts the indicative.

sections.heading: Ojalá: three tenses, three feelings
sections.body: Choose the tense by how real the wish is. Present subjunctive for a hopeful future, imperfect subjunctive for a wish against present reality, pluperfect subjunctive for a regret about the past:

ex.en: I wish I could help you.

sections.heading: Ojalá for regret: the pluperfect subjunctive
sections.body: To wish the past had gone differently, use ojalá + hubiera + participle. This is pure regret — it can't be changed now:

ex.en: I wish he had come to the party.
I wish I had known it earlier.

sections.heading: Como si: always past subjunctive
sections.body: Como si introduces something contrary to fact, so it takes the imperfect subjunctive (as if it were now) or the pluperfect subjunctive (as if it had happened). Never the present, never the indicative:

ex.en: He talks as if he were an expert.

ex.es: Me miró como si no me hubiera visto nunca.
ex.en: He looked at me as if he had never seen me.

takeaways: Ojalá + present subjunctive = hopeful future: Ojalá venga.
Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = wish against present reality: Ojalá viniera / pudiera.
Ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive = past regret: Ojalá hubiera venido.
Como si ALWAYS takes the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive: como si fuera, como si hubiera visto.

mistakes.why: Como si never takes the present or indicative; it needs a past subjunctive: fuera.
Como si always takes the imperfect subjunctive here: fueras.
Ojalá takes the subjunctive, never the indicative: venga.

exercises.no: Ojalá takes the subjunctive; for a hopeful future use “venga”.

exercises.prompt_en: He talks as if he were an expert.
exercises.no: Como si always takes a past subjunctive: “fuera”, never “es” or “sea”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I wish he had come to the party.”
exercises.no: “Ojalá hubiera venido a la fiesta” — a past regret needs the pluperfect subjunctive.

exercises.prompt_en: You spend as if you were rich.
exercises.hint: Como si + imperfect subjunctive of ser (tú).
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Como si + imperfecto de subjuntivo → fueras.
exercises.no: Como si takes the imperfect subjunctive: “fueras”.

exercises.prompt: Match each expression to its meaning.

exercises.translation: I wish I could help you.
exercises.no: It was: “Ojalá pudiera ayudarte.” (I wish I could help you.)

exercises.scenario: Talking about a friend who acts arrogant 😒

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Have you seen how Luis behaves?

options.text: Sí, actúa como si lo supiera todo.
Sí, actúa como si lo sabe todo.
Sí, actúa como si lo sepa todo.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Como si + imperfecto de subjuntivo → supiera.
exercises.no: Como si needs a past subjunctive: “como si lo supiera todo”.

exercises.en: He talks as if he were an expert.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Habla como si fuera experto.”
